CHAPTER 2 — DATA MANAGEMENT,
BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE AND AI ANALYTICS
2.1 Database Management Systems, Data Warehousing, Data
Marts and Big Data
1. What is Data?
Data means raw facts and figures that can be collected, stored and processed.
Examples
● Student name: Kevin
● Age: 24
● Marks: 85
● Product price: ₹500
● Number of products sold: 150
● Customer location: Mumbai
By themselves, these values may not tell us much.
Data vs Information
Data → Raw facts
Information → Meaningful data obtained after processing
Example
Suppose a shop has this data:
Product Sale
s
Laptop 50
Mobile 120
Headphone
s
80
This is data.
After analyzing it, we can say:

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
"Mobile phones are the best-selling product."
That conclusion is information.
Simple way to remember
Data → Processing → Information
2. What is a Database?
A database is an organized collection of data that can be easily stored, accessed, managed and updated.
Example
A university may maintain a database containing:
● Student ID
● Student name
● Course
● Semester
● Marks
● Attendance
● Contact information
Instead of maintaining thousands of records in separate files, the university can store them in a database.
3. What is DBMS?
DBMS = Database Management System
A DBMS is software used to create, store, organize, retrieve, update and manage data in a database.
Examples of DBMS
● MySQL
● Oracle Database
● Microsoft SQL Server
● PostgreSQL
● MongoDB
Example
Imagine a college has 10,000 students.
The college needs to:

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
● Add new students
● Update student information
● Find a particular student
● Calculate marks
● Delete old records
● Generate reports
A DBMS makes these operations easier.
4. Main Functions of DBMS
A DBMS performs several important functions.
1. Data Storage
It stores large amounts of data in an organized way.
2. Data Retrieval
It allows users to find required information quickly.
Example:
Find all students who scored more than 80 marks.
3. Data Modification
Users can update existing information.
Example:
Changing a student's phone number.
4. Data Deletion
Unnecessary records can be removed.
5. Security
A DBMS can control who can access particular data.
For example:
● Student → Can see own marks
● Teacher → Can see students' marks
● Administrator → Can modify student records
6. Data Integrity

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
It helps maintain accurate and consistent data.
7. Backup and Recovery
Data can be backed up and recovered if something goes wrong.
5. Why Do Businesses Need DBMS?
Businesses generate huge amounts of data every day.
For example, Amazon may store information about:
● Customers
● Products
● Orders
● Payments
● Deliveries
● Reviews
A DBMS helps the company manage this information efficiently.
Business Example
Suppose a customer orders a laptop.
The database records:
Customer → Order → Product → Payment → Delivery
All these records can be connected and managed through a database system.
6. Data Warehousing
A Data Warehouse is a large centralized repository used to store data collected from different sources for
analysis and reporting.
The important point is:
Database → Mainly used for daily operations
Data Warehouse → Mainly used for analysis and decision-making
Example
A supermarket may have separate systems for:
● Billing

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
● Online orders
● Customer loyalty cards
● Inventory
● Suppliers
The company can collect data from all these systems and put it into a data warehouse.
Then managers can analyze:
● Monthly sales
● Most popular products
● Customer buying patterns
● Sales by region
● Yearly growth
7.
Database vs Data WarehouseEasy example
When you buy something from Amazon:
Database:
"Kevin purchased a laptop today."
Data Warehouse:
"Customers aged 18–30 purchased 35% more laptops this year than last year."
The first is an operation.
The second is analysis.
Database Data Warehouse
Used mainly for daily operations Used mainly for analysis
Frequently updated Mainly stores historical data
Handles transactions Handles analytical queries
Used by operational staff Used by managers/analysts
Example: placing an order Example: analyzing 5 years of
sales

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
8. Data Mart
A Data Mart is a smaller part of a data warehouse designed for a particular department or business
function.
Example
A large company may have one Data Warehouse containing company-wide data.
From it, different departments may have their own data marts:
Data Warehouse
↓
● Sales Data Mart
● Finance Data Mart
● Marketing Data Mart
● HR Data Mart
Example
The Marketing Data Mart may contain:
● Customer demographics
● Advertising campaigns
● Website visits
● Sales generated by campaigns
The marketing department doesn't need all the company's financial or HR information.
Therefore, a Data Mart gives the department the specific data it needs.
9. Data Warehouse vs Data Mart
Data Warehouse Data Mart
Large Smaller
Organization-wide Department-specific
Contains data from many
areas
Focuses on one area
Used for overall analysis Used for specific analysis
Easy memory trick
Warehouse = Whole organization
Mart = Particular department

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
Source: jpaw-ayto-zafra
10. Big Data
Big Data refers to extremely large, complex and rapidly generated datasets that traditional
data-processing systems may struggle to handle.
Examples
Think about YouTube, Instagram, Amazon or Google.
Every day they generate enormous amounts of:
● Text
● Images
● Videos
● Transactions
● Search queries
● Customer reviews
● Location data
● Clicks
This is Big Data.

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
Source: usdsi.org
11. Characteristics of Big Data — The 5 Vs
A very important concept for exams is the 5 Vs of Big Data.
1. Volume
Means the huge amount of data.
Example
Facebook stores enormous amounts of photos, videos and messages.
Volume = How much data?
2. Velocity
Means the speed at which data is generated and processed.
Example
Stock market prices change every second.
Velocity = How fast is data generated?

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
3. Variety
Means the different types and formats of data.
Examples:
● Text
● Images
● Videos
● Audio
● Numbers
● Social media posts
Variety = What types of data?
4. Veracity
Means the accuracy, reliability and trustworthiness of data.
For example, imagine 1,000 customers provide their age.
Some people may enter:
● 25
● 26
● 250
● "I don't know"
The company needs to identify unreliable data.
Veracity = Can we trust the data?
5. Value
Means the useful information or benefit obtained from data.
Collecting billions of records is useless if the company cannot use them to make better decisions.
Value = Can we get something useful from the data?
Easy way to remember:
5 Vs = Volume + Velocity + Variety + Veracity + Value

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
2.2 Business Intelligence, Data Visualization,
AI and Predictive Analytics, Decision Support
Systems
12. What is Business Intelligence?
Business Intelligence (BI) refers to technologies, processes and methods used to collect, analyze and
present business data so that organizations can make better decisions.
In simple words:
BI converts business data into useful information for decision-making.
Example
A company has thousands of sales records.
BI can help answer:
● Which product sells the most?
● Which city generates the highest sales?
● Which month has the highest revenue?
● Which products are losing popularity?
13. How Business Intelligence Works
A simple BI process is:
Data Collection
↓
Data Storage
↓
Data Analysis
↓
Data Visualization
↓
Business Decision

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
Example
A clothing company collects sales data.
The BI system discovers:
Sales of winter jackets increased by 40% in December.
The manager can then decide:
Increase jacket inventory before next winter.
So:
Data → Analysis → Insight → Decision
14. Benefits of Business Intelligence
Source: wvtc

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
15. What is Data Visualization?
Data Visualization means representing data using visual formats such as:
● Charts
● Graphs
● Tables
● Maps
● Dashboards
Instead of looking at thousands of numbers, visualization allows users to understand patterns quickly.
Source: fitly

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
Example
Imagine these sales figures:
January → ₹20,000
February → ₹25,000
March → ₹40,000
April → ₹60,000
A graph immediately shows that sales are increasing.
This is much easier to understand than reading hundreds of numbers.

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
16. Common Types of Data Visualization
1. Bar Chart
Useful for comparing categories.
Example
Compare sales of:
● Laptop
● Mobile
● Tablet
● Headphones
2. Line Chart
Useful for showing changes over time.
Example
Monthly revenue from January to December.
3. Pie Chart
Useful for showing proportions or percentages.
Example
A company's market share:
● Company A → 40%
● Company B → 30%
● Company C → 20%
● Others → 10%
4. Map
Useful for geographical information.
Example

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
A company can display sales by:
● Mumbai
● Delhi
● Bangalore
● Chennai
5. Dashboard
A dashboard combines multiple visualizations in one place.
For example:
Sales Dashboard
● Total Sales
● Total Customers
● Best-Selling Product
● Monthly Revenue
● Regional Sales
This allows a manager to understand the business quickly.
17. What is AI Analytics?
AI Analytics uses Artificial Intelligence techniques to analyze data and generate insights, predictions or
recommendations.
Traditional analytics might ask:
"What happened?"
AI analytics can go further and ask:
"Why did it happen?"
and
"What is likely to happen next?"

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
18. Predictive Analytics
Predictive Analytics uses historical data, statistical methods and AI/machine learning techniques to
predict future outcomes.
Example
A company has sales data from the last five years.
The system analyzes:
● Previous sales
● Seasonal patterns
● Customer behavior
● Prices
● Marketing campaigns
It may predict:
"Sales are likely to increase next month."
The company can then prepare additional stock.

20. Real-Life Examples of Predictive Analytics
Banking
Predict whether a customer may fail to repay a loan.
E-commerce
Predict which products a customer may purchase.
Healthcare
Predict possible health risks based on available data.
Manufacturing
Predict when a machine may fail.
Retail
Predict future product demand.

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
21. Decision Support System (DSS)
A Decision Support System (DSS) is a computer-based system that helps managers make decisions by
analyzing data and presenting useful information.
It does not necessarily make the final decision for the manager.
Instead, it provides information that helps the manager make a better decision.
Example
Suppose a company wants to open a new store.
A DSS can analyze:
● Population
● Customer income
● Existing competitors
● Previous sales
● Location
● Customer demand
The system may show:
Location A has the highest potential.
The manager then decides whether to open the store.

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
22. DSS Example — Simple Scenario
Imagine a food delivery company wants to decide where to open a new restaurant branch.
The DSS analyzes:
● Number of customers
● Average order value
● Competitor restaurants
● Delivery times
● Population
● Historical demand
The system provides a recommendation.
Manager → Uses DSS → Makes decision

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia

2.3 Generative AI Tools for Business Reporting
and Analytics
The syllabus specifically includes Generative AI tools for business reporting and analytics and
mentions tools such as Power BI, Tableau and Google Looker Studio.
24. What is Generative AI?
Generative AI is a type of AI that can generate new content based on user instructions and available
information.
It can generate:
● Text
● Reports
● Summaries
● Images
● Code
● Explanations
● Business insights
Business Example
A manager provides sales data and asks an AI system:
"Summarize the sales performance for this month."
The system can generate a summary of the important trends.
25. Generative AI in Business Analytics
Generative AI can help businesses with:
1. Report Generation
It can help create business reports from data.
2. Data Summarization
It can summarize large datasets or analytical results.
3. Insight Generation
It can help identify important trends and patterns.

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
4. Natural Language Queries
Instead of writing complex queries, a user can ask:
"Show me the sales of laptops in Mumbai."
5. Presentation of Results
AI can help explain complex analytical results in simple language.

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
26. Power BI
Microsoft Power BI is a business intelligence and data visualization platform.
It can be used to:
● Connect to data
● Transform data
● Analyze data
● Create charts
● Create dashboards
● Generate reports
● Share business insights
Example
A company imports its sales data into Power BI.
It can create a dashboard showing:
Total Revenue: ₹50 lakh
Total Orders: 12,000
Best Product: Laptop
Best Region: Mumbai
Monthly Sales Trend
This allows managers to understand business performance quickly.

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
27. Tableau
Tableau is a data visualization and business analytics platform used to create interactive charts,
dashboards and reports.
Example
A retail company can use Tableau to visualize:
● Sales by region
● Customer demographics
● Product performance
● Monthly revenue
● Profit trends
Users can interact with the dashboard and filter the information.

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
28. Google Looker Studio
Google Looker Studio is a reporting and data visualization tool that can be used to create interactive
dashboards and reports.
It can connect with different data sources and present the information visually.
Example
A digital marketing company can create a dashboard showing:
● Website visitors
● Advertising performance
● Click-through rate
● Conversion rate
● Revenue

Mr. Dhrupesh Savadia
29. Power BI vs Tableau vs Looker Studio
Tool Main Use
Power BI BI, analytics and dashboards
Tableau Data visualization and analytics
Google Looker Studio Reporting and interactive

For your students, don't make them memorize too many technical differences unless the teacher

These tools help transform business data into understandable reports, visualizations
